newsitem.title: RUSSIA: General Electric in Russian engines venture.
newsitem.headline: General Electric in Russian engines venture.

text.p: Russian aircraft engine manufacturer AO Rybinskiye Motory and GE Aircraft Engines, a division of U.S. General Electric Co, have begun a joint venture to produce spare parts for aircraft and industrial engines.

Rybinsk Motors general director Valery Shelgunov told Reuters in Rybinsk, 300 km northeast of Moscow, on Wednesday the new firm would produce spare parts for CT-7 engines which power Russian's new Sukhoi S-80 turboprop aircraft and Kamov Ka-64 helicopters.

"We have got access to GE high technologies and we will use them in our production," Shelgunov said, adding that the joint venture also would produce industrial LM-2500 engines, often used for gas pumps.
Tracey Homburg, GE vice-president and director of market development for the CIS, said Rybinsk Motors was chosen from two other Russian engine makers.
"We see a joint business as promising," he said.
Rybinsk Motors has been already producing spare parts for GE-made aircraft and industrial engines. Company officials did not give the production volume.
Shelgunov said the venture's charter capital was $600,000.
"Each partner invested half of this sum," he added.
Homburg was appointed general director for two years.
